newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's BASF to cut sick pay benefits.
newsitem.headline: Germany's BASF to cut sick pay benefits.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG, following the lead of Daimler-Benz AG, said on Wednesday that it would cut sick pay benefits beginning October 1.
"We also want to curb sick pay beginning on October 1," a BASF spokesman told Reuters in answer to an enquiry.

Daimler said on Tuesday it would implement controversial new legislation to cut sick pay to 80 percent from Oct 1 despite unions and some leading politicians saying companies had no right to make such cutbacks so quickly.
Daimler works council chairman Karl Feuerstein told journalists on Wednesday that the council board had voted in favour of not working overtime shifts due to the changes.

Unions and some top politicians have said companies do not have the right to make the sickpay cutback, and that the bill passed by parliament earlier this month was not meant to apply to existing contracts, only future ones.

But Daimler and other industrial leaders have taken a sharply different view and intend to use the legislation, which is part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's programme to boost sagging unemployment, to reopen talks with unions on cutting costs.
